_doc: Named render recipes for tools/h3-rapid.sh: `tools/h3-rapid.sh --profile NAME`.
A profile is applied as defaults before any flag, so an explicit flag on the
command line still wins; a profile does win over the environment's
H3_DIT_GEMM/H3_VAE_GEMM/H3_VAE_ATTENTION, because choosing a profile is an
explicit act and the shell's leftovers are not. The resolved values are
printed on the PLAN lines of every render, so a clip always records its own
recipe. Keys are the script's own flags; `doc` is for --list-profiles.
A profile may carry `prompt` or `prompt_file`, which makes it a whole shot and not only its settings; an explicit -p still wins.

The `quality-*` profiles are the reference's own rule for a face or a moving camera: one stage at full size rather than a 0.7 draft, whose small canvas is what gives up close-up detail; they also trade the `bf16a` decode for the reference-faithful `bf16i` one and encode at crf 12/veryslow.

The `master` pair goes one step further on the same canvas: crf 6 on veryslow and the reference's Fp32 decode. `master` also drops the fp8 arm (the largest picture change there is, 21.7 dB), while `master-fp8` keeps it so the latent is the one `quality-portrait` already produced. Neither is a larger canvas: the engine refuses anything over the released 768*1344 pixel limit (render.rs), which is why no 2K or 4K profile exists.

ts_h2.doc: The reference's default preset (Rapid-H3 harness/workflow.py:50-52: steps=6, draft 0.7, refine_sigmas 0.72 0, freeze_audio, encode_once). Best quality of the route family; 12.3 s a draft step plus a 38.4 s refine step.

rapid.doc: The speed point: the same route at 4 draft steps. -25.4 s of wall and -10.2% detail energy against ts_h2, and the clip gate passes (four-step-draft-2026-11-02.md).

rapid-e4m3.doc: rapid with the draft leg on the E4M3 attention arm: draft -7.1%, gate exit 0, delivered audio +1.55 dB (draft-fp8-attention-2026-11-02.md). Opt-in for that reason.

one-pass.doc: The reference's ts_s6 shape: no draft, no upscale, one stage at full size. Stock-level camera moves and close-up faces, 347.6 s at five seconds; the arm to reach for on a push-in or a beauty close-up.

portrait.doc: The same speed point at 9:16. Draft lands at 544x928 (0.7 of 768x1344, rounded to /32) and the delivery at 768x1344; nothing else moves.

ipanema.doc: The Ipanema shot: portrait canvas, four steps, the scene baked into the profile. No lyric text in this file - it is the song's and not this repository's - so a render that has to sing specific words passes them with --prompt-file, which wins over the profile's prompt. Rendered at 167.3 s without lyrics, md5 7b2caec8d8611c86f594d066675e73e7.
ipanema.prompt: A Brazilian woman in a thong bikini walks across the wet sand on Ipanema beach in Rio de Janeiro at golden hour, medium close-up, 9:16 portrait framing, ocean and the Two Brothers mountain behind her, warm low sunlight, light wind in her hair. She looks straight into the camera, smiling, and sings in Portuguese with a soft bossa nova voice, her lips moving in time with the words.

quality-portrait.doc: Highest quality at 9:16, by the reference's own rule: a close-up or a face goes on the one-stage preset (its ts_s6) rather than a 0.7 draft, because the small draft gives up close-up detail (README:116,172). Six steps at full canvas, the reference's decode numerics (vae_gemm bf16i, no rounding arm), crf 12 on the veryslow preset. About 320 s for five seconds against 167 s on `portrait`.

quality.doc: Highest quality at 16:9: one stage at full canvas, six steps, the reference's decode numerics (vae_gemm bf16i, no rounding arm), crf 12 on the veryslow preset. The reference's ts_s6 shape, which is the one it recommends when motion or a face matters (README:116). About 330 s for five seconds against 181 s on `rapid`.

master.doc: The cleanest picture the released canvas allows: one stage at 768x1344, six steps, and the reference's BF16 projection arithmetic instead of the fp8 arm - fp8 measures 21.7 dB from bf16, which is a different picture and not a noisy one - with the reference's decode numerics (fp32, tensor attention, tile 320) and crf 6 on veryslow. It is a different sample from `quality-portrait` because the generator's arm changed; about 6.5 min for five seconds.

master-fp8.doc: The clip `quality-portrait` already made - the fp8 arm, the same seed, so the denoised latent is the same - decoded and encoded as cleanly as the pipeline can: fp32 decode at the reference's tile, crf 6/veryslow. This redoes the pixels of a shot you already have; `master` is the more faithful sample instead. About 6 min for five seconds.

ts_h.doc: The reference's earlier preset, kept for detail rather than speed: two refine steps at the delivery canvas (refine_sigmas 0.78, 0.45, 0) instead of one, on the same 0.7 draft, at 9:16 with the reference's decode numerics and crf 12/veryslow. More detail at the same canvas; about 38 s more than `quality-portrait`.
